public_rationale: A contemporaneous evaluation found repeated incorrect factual answers across several frontier models. That supports the ordinary claim that hallucinations remained a recurring problem. Its deliberately difficult questions do not establish how frequently an average user encountered hallucinations.
limitations: SimpleQA selects difficult questions and tests short answers without browsing.
The evaluation was conducted by a model developer and uses automated grading with human checks.
The paper does not give exact execution dates; event_date therefore uses year precision.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations are still a regular occurrence in LLMs.

statement.excerpt: Instead, hallucinations are still a regular occurrence.

our_interpretation: Regular means recurring factual fabrications across systematic evaluations of contemporary LLMs. It does not mean that most responses hallucinate.

The reference to the latest 2024 edition anchors the observation to 2024 through publication. I use that current-year reporting window because model evaluations have no standard quarterly reporting cycle.
Benchmark frequencies establish recurring failures in the tested tasks, not a population-wide rate for everyday conversations.
criteria.support_condition: Systematic evaluations during the target period find repeated false or unsupported factual answers from contemporary, widely used LLMs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, representative evaluations establish that hallucinations have become exceptional, isolated failures across contemporary LLMs and ordinary factual tasks.
